correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the adjacency spectra and parity factors from exact Cartesian coordinates: with antipodes ordered in pairs, adjacency has blocks (B,C;C,B), and B+C and B-C have exactly the even and odd characteristic-polynomial factors in the table. Independently checked the unique graph-distance antipode for each vertex and the degree-three geometric eigenspace (eigenvalues 1, 0, sqrt(5), sqrt(5) on cube, octahedron, icosahedron, dodecahedron). Its projector has entries 3(u·v)/(N r^2), with r the vertex radius, so strict Cauchy–Schwarz excludes PGST for every distinct non-antipodal pair; the tetrahedron follows from A=J-I. The bounded exact reproduction is replayable with python -B /workspace/branches/platonic_reconstruction.py (SymPy); it passed the four parity, shell and geometric projector checks and both derivative and peak-value identities. The uploaded scripts were inspected but not run. Vertex transitivity gives diagonal weights m_lambda/N and hence the stated amplitudes. For the dodecahedron the two frequencies 1 and sqrt(5) have dense joint phase torus; strict convexity in cos(sqrt(5)t) reduces to endpoints. The negative endpoint has squared numerator at most 144, and the positive endpoint polynomial has only one interior stationary point x=-1/2, where the derivative changes from positive to negative and the squared numerator is 243. Equality additionally requires sqrt(5)t/(2pi) integral, impossible for nonzero rational t/(2pi) giving cos t=-1/2. For icosahedral antipodes odd Pell indices give q even, p odd, p-sqrt(5)q=1/(p+sqrt(5)q); evaluating at t=pi q gives the stated cos^4 limit. Exact transfer would require 6t and 2sqrt(5)t to be multiples of 2pi, which forces t=0 and fails the parity-phase condition. The single-frequency cube, octahedron and tetrahedron attain the stated values at pi/2, pi/3 and pi/4.
